draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Fort Aguada! The Portuguese built this fort in 1612, together with a lighthouse, right on Sinquerim Beach looking out over the Arabian Sea. It's now protected as a Monument of National Importance.
draft.hungryLine: No eateries in my notes around the fort, so ask nearby in Sinquerim what's fresh today.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The fort is about a 20 minute walk from here, and Sinquerim beach is about 22 minutes away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Head down to the crescent of sand at Sinquerim and watch the Arabian Sea.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Taj resort here was once called the Fort Aguada Beach Resort, and its 56-acre grounds even include cricket grounds.

spots.name: Houses of Goa Museum
spots.detail: In Salvador-do-Mundo, Bardez · Gerard da Cunha's museum on how Goan homes mix East and West

tips.title: Treat the fort gently.
tips.body: It's an ASI protected Monument of National Importance, so don't climb or scratch the walls.

tips.title: Plan for museum days.
tips.body: The Houses of Goa Museum opens Tuesday to Sunday, 10 AM to 7:30 PM.

story.title: A fort with a light
story.body: The Portuguese built Fort Aguada and its lighthouse in 1612 on Sinquerim Beach, overlooking the Arabian Sea.

story.title: A resort on the crescent
story.body: A beach resort grew up on the curve of the beach at Sinquerim. Once named the Fort Aguada Beach Resort, it's now the Taj Fort Aguada Resort & Spa.

story.title: A national monument
story.body: The fort is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India as a Monument of National Importance.
